questions.question: Suppose a triangular object (O) is placed in front of a plane mirror and its image is observed at position (X). Which one of the following diagrams represents the image (I) formed by the mirror when it is observed from position (X)?

options.A: Diagram A
options.B: Diagram B
options.C: Diagram C
options.D: Diagram D

questions.explanation: In a plane mirror, the image formed is virtual, upright, and laterally inverted. The image appears to be behind the mirror at the same distance as the object is in front. The image is also reversed from left to right. The correct diagram would show the image behind the mirror, with the same size and orientation but reversed.

questions.question: An object is placed 25.0 cm in front of a concave mirror having focal length of 10.0 cm. The magnification of the mirror is
questions.explanation: Using the mirror equation: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f = 10 cm and u = -25 cm (object distance is negative for mirrors using sign convention). 1/v = 1/10 - 1/25 = (5-2)/50 = 3/50, so v = 50/3 ≈ 16.7 cm. Magnification m = -v/u = -(16.7)/(-25) = -0.67. The negative sign indicates the image is inverted. The magnitude of magnification is 0.67.

questions.question: Which of the following statements distinguishes between random and systematic errors?

options.A: Systematic error can be minimized by taking several readings and averaging; whereas random error cannot be minimized.
options.B: Systematic error makes measured values to be always above or always below the true value; whereas random error causes measured values to be sometimes above and sometimes below the true value.
options.C: Random error makes measured values to be always above or always below the true value; whereas systematic error causes measured values to be sometimes above and sometimes below the true value.
options.D: Random error is biased, whereas systematic error does not show bias.

questions.explanation: Systematic errors are consistent, repeatable errors that cause measurements to be consistently higher or lower than the true value (bias). Random errors are unpredictable fluctuations that cause measurements to be sometimes higher and sometimes lower than the true value, averaging out over many measurements. Taking multiple readings and averaging helps minimize random errors, not systematic errors.

questions.question: The unit vector in the direction of A = 3i + 4j is

options.B: 2i - j
options.D: i + j

questions.explanation: A unit vector in the direction of a vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of vector A = 3i + 4j is √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5. Therefore, the unit vector = (3i+4j)/5 = (3/5)i + (4/5)j. This vector has magnitude 1 and points in the same direction as the original vector.

questions.question: Which of the following pair of vectors are collinear?

options.A: 2i - 3j and -4i - 6j
options.B: i + j and -i + j
options.C: 2i + 3j and -4i + 6j
options.D: 2i + 3j and -4i - 6j

questions.explanation: Two vectors are collinear if one is a scalar multiple of the other. For option D: -4i - 6j = -2(2i + 3j), so they are scalar multiples of each other. For option A: -4i - 6j = -2(2i) + 2(-3j), not a scalar multiple. Option B: i+j and -i+j are not scalar multiples. Option C: 2i+3j and -4i+6j are not scalar multiples.

questions.question: For an object moving in straight line,

options.A: if the displacement changes by equal amount in equal time interval, the displacement-time graph is horizontal line.
options.B: the area of the region under the displacement-time graph and the slope of velocity-time graph are, respectively, the acceleration and displacement of the object.
options.C: if the velocity increases by equal amount in equal time interval, the velocity-time graph is straight line with positive slope and the acceleration-time graph is horizontal.
options.D: the slope of displacement-time graph and the area of the region under acceleration-time graph are, respectively, the acceleration and velocity of the object.

questions.explanation: If velocity increases by equal amounts in equal time intervals (uniform acceleration), the velocity-time graph is a straight line with constant positive slope (the acceleration). The acceleration-time graph is a horizontal line (constant acceleration). Option A is incorrect: displacement increasing equally gives a straight line with positive slope, not horizontal. Option B: slope of displacement-time graph gives velocity, not acceleration. Option D: slope of displacement-time gives velocity, not acceleration.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about satellite motion?

options.A: A satellite moving closer to the Earth takes longer time to complete one revolution than a satellite farther from the Earth.
options.B: For two satellites moving around the Earth at equal orbital radius, a heavier satellite has larger speed than a lighter one.
options.C: For equal orbital radius, a satellite moving around the Earth has smaller speed than a satellite moving about Moon.
options.D: A satellite closer to Earth is faster than a satellite farther from the Earth.

questions.explanation: According to Kepler's laws and the orbital speed equation v = √(GM/r), a satellite's orbital speed increases as it moves closer to the central body. Therefore, a satellite closer to Earth has a higher speed and a shorter orbital period. Option A is incorrect because closer satellites have shorter periods. Option B is incorrect because orbital speed is independent of satellite mass. Option C is incorrect because the Earth has greater mass than the Moon, so the speed would be greater for Earth orbit at the same radius.

questions.question: A block of mass m is placed on horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is μ. A force of magnitude F acts on the block at an angle θ as shown in the figure below. The minimum magnitude of the force F required to slide the block on the surface is

options.A: μmg/(cosθ - μsinθ)
options.B: μmg/(cosθ + μsinθ)
options.C: μmg/(cosθ - sinθ)
options.D: μmg/(cosθ + sinθ)

questions.explanation: When a force F is applied at an angle θ below the horizontal (as shown in the figure), the vertical component Fsinθ increases the normal force: N = mg + Fsinθ. The maximum static friction is f = μN = μ(mg + Fsinθ). To just start moving, the horizontal component of F must equal the friction force: Fcosθ = μ(mg + Fsinθ). Solving for F: Fcosθ = μmg + μFsinθ, Fcosθ - μFsinθ = μmg, F(cosθ - μsinθ) = μmg, F = μmg/(cosθ - μsinθ).

questions.question: A ball of mass m moving with a speed v strikes a hard wall at an angle θ with the wall. It is reflected with the same speed at the same angle as shown in the figure below. If the ball is in contact with the wall for time t, then the average force acting on the wall is given by

options.A: (mv/t)cosθ
options.B: (mv/t)sinθ
options.C: (2mv/t)cosθ
options.D: (2mv/t)sinθ

questions.explanation: When a ball strikes a wall at an angle and reflects with the same speed and angle, only the perpendicular component of momentum changes. The parallel component remains unchanged. The change in momentum in the perpendicular direction is: Δp = p_final - p_initial = mv sinθ - (-mv sinθ) = 2mv sinθ (taking direction into account). By the impulse-momentum theorem: F_avg × t = Δp = 2mv sinθ. Therefore, F_avg = (2mv/t)sinθ. This force is exerted by the wall on the ball, and by Newton's third law, the ball exerts an equal and opposite force on the wall.

questions.question: According to the Heisenberg's uncertainty principle,

options.A: the larger the position uncertainty, the larger the momentum uncertainty.
options.B: if the uncertainty in position decreases, the momentum uncertainty decreases, too.
options.C: the more precisely we measure the position of a particle; we become less precise of its momentum and vice versa.
options.D: we can measure both the position and momentum of a particle simultaneously with unlimited precision.

questions.explanation: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states that there is a fundamental limit to the precision with which certain pairs of physical properties (like position and momentum) can be known simultaneously. The product of the uncertainties in position (Δx) and momentum (Δp) must be greater than or equal to ħ/2. Therefore, if position is measured with high precision (small Δx), the momentum uncertainty (Δp) must be large, and vice versa.

questions.question: The graph of nuclear binding energy per nucleon (BE/A) versus mass number (A) has its peak near an atomic weight A = 56. Which of the following statements is true about the graph?

options.A: Uranium (A = 235), which has larger binding energy than iron (A= 56), is more stable than iron.
options.B: Nucleus with larger number of neutron is more stable than nucleus of the same atom with smaller number of neutron.
options.C: For heavier nuclei (A > 56), the binding energy per nucleon decreases with the increase of mass number; implying that heavier atoms can increase their stability by increasing their protons' number.
options.D: For smaller atoms (A < 56), the binding energy per nucleon generally increases with the increase of mass number; indicating that lighter atoms can increase stability through nuclear fission.

questions.explanation: The binding energy per nucleon increases up to A ≈ 56 (iron), then decreases for heavier nuclei. For smaller atoms (A < 56), fusion of lighter nuclei into heavier ones increases binding energy per nucleon, leading to greater stability. For heavier atoms (A > 56), fission increases stability. Option A is incorrect: although uranium has larger total binding energy, its binding energy per nucleon is smaller, making it less stable.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about reflection and refraction of sound waves and their applications?

options.A: In pre-natal scanning, reflection and refraction of sound allows doctors to monitor the progress of a developing baby.
options.B: Reflection of sound (echo) is formed when sound enters a medium of varying densities.
options.C: Reflection and refraction of sound are used to detect flaws in metals and to help people park their cars.
options.D: Refraction of sound is the change in its direction as it travels through a medium having different densities.

questions.explanation: Option B is NOT correct because reflection of sound (echo) occurs when sound waves bounce off a surface, not when they enter a medium of varying densities. When sound enters a medium of varying densities, it undergoes refraction (change in direction), not reflection. Prenatal scanning (ultrasound) uses both reflection and refraction. Sonar and ultrasonic testing also use sound reflection and refraction.

questions.question: A torque τ rotates an object of mass m and moment of inertia I through an angle θ. The work done on the object by the torque is

options.B: mθ
options.C: τθ
options.D: τI

questions.explanation: The work done by a torque is given by the product of the torque and the angular displacement: W = τ × θ. This is analogous to the linear case where work = force × distance. This formula applies when the torque is constant and acts through an angular displacement θ. The moment of inertia I is related to rotational kinetic energy but does not appear in the work formula for a constant torque.

questions.question: A satellite revolves around the Earth in a circular orbit of radius r = 4 × 10¹⁶ m. The period of the satellite is
questions.explanation: Using Kepler's third law: T² = (4π²/GM)r³. With M_Earth = 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg², and r = 4 × 10¹⁶ m. T² = 4π² × (4 × 10¹⁶)³ / (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 5.97 × 10²⁴) = 39.48 × 6.4 × 10⁴⁹ / (3.98 × 10¹⁴) = 6.35 × 10³⁶, T = √(6.35 × 10³⁶) = 2.52 × 10¹⁸ s. However, option A is 2.5 × 10¹⁹ s. This discrepancy may arise from using different values or a different interpretation. Based on the given answer, option A is correct as per the exam key.

questions.question: Two resistors R₁ = 1Ω and R₂ = 4Ω are connected in parallel to each other and their combination is connected in series with a third resistor R₃ = 2Ω. The whole combination is connected to a voltage source of potential difference 14 V. The potential difference across R₁ is

options.C: 5 V
options.D: 4 V

questions.explanation: First, find the equivalent resistance of R₁ and R₂ in parallel: 1/R_parallel = 1/1 + 1/4 = 5/4, so R_parallel = 0.8Ω. Total resistance = R_parallel + R₃ = 0.8 + 2 = 2.8Ω. Total current I = V/R = 14/2.8 = 5 A. The voltage across the parallel combination = I × R_parallel = 5 × 0.8 = 4 V. Since R₁ and R₂ are in parallel, they have the same potential difference of 4 V. Therefore, the potential difference across R₁ is 4 V.

questions.question: Consider a long and tightly wound solenoid carrying current I, having length L and N turns of winding. If n is the number of turns per unit length, which of the following describes the magnetic field produced by the solenoid?

options.A: The magnetic field inside the solenoid is zero, whereas the field outside is perpendicular to the length of the solenoid.
options.B: The magnetic field inside the solenoid is constant and is parallel to the solenoid's axis, whereas the field outside is negligible.
options.C: The magnetic field inside the solenoid is uniform and perpendicular to the axis of the solenoid.
options.D: The magnetic field outside the solenoid is as strong as the field inside it.

questions.explanation: For an ideal solenoid, the magnetic field inside is uniform (constant) and directed parallel to the axis of the solenoid. The field outside is nearly zero (negligible) for a long solenoid. The field is given by B = μ₀nI, where n is the number of turns per unit length. Option B correctly describes both the inside and outside field characteristics.

questions.question: According to the law of electromagnetic induction,

options.A: the magnitude of emf induced in a circuit is directly proportional to the rate of change the magnetic flux crossing any surface bounded by the circuit.
options.B: a changing magnetic field parallel to the plane of a circuit induces an emf in it.
options.C: a constant magnetic flux crossing the surface of a circuit induced an emf in the circuit.
options.D: an emf is induced in a circuit when a constant magnetic field crosses its surface.

questions.explanation: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the magnitude of the induced emf is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit: ε = -dΦ/dt. A changing magnetic field induces emf, but it must have a component perpendicular to the plane of the circuit to change the flux. A constant flux or constant magnetic field crossing the surface does not induce emf.

questions.question: A resistor R, a capacitor C, and inductor L are connected in series to an AC voltage source that generates a sinusoidal voltage, V(t) = V_p sin(ωt), with V_p and ω being the peak voltage and angular frequency of the source. If X_C, X_L, and Z are capacitive reactance, inductive reactance, and impedance, respectively; I_rms and V_rms are the root-mean-square (rms) values of the current and voltage, the average power dissipated in series the RLC circuit is given by

options.A: 2I_p V_p R/√(R² + (X_L - X_C)²)
options.B: I_rms V_rms
options.C: I_rms V_rms R/√(R² + (X_L - X_C)²)
options.D: I_rms² Z

questions.explanation: The average power dissipated in an AC circuit is P_avg = V_rms I_rms cosφ, where cosφ = R/Z is the power factor. Z = √(R² + (X_L - X_C)²). Therefore, P_avg = I_rms V_rms × R/Z = I_rms V_rms R/√(R² + (X_L - X_C)²). Option A uses peak values incorrectly. Option B gives apparent power, not average power. Option D gives apparent power using impedance.

options.A: the larger the position uncertainty, the larger the momentum uncertainty.
options.B: if the uncertainty in position decreases, the momentum uncertainty decreases, too.
options.C: the more precisely we measure the position of a particle; we become less precise of its momentum and vice versa.

questions.question: One of the following statements is a correct description of the charging processes?

options.A: During charging a neutral object by induction using a negatively charged rod, charge flows from the rod to the object.
options.B: When a neutral metallic sphere is charged by induction using a negatively charged rod, the sphere acquires a net negative charge.
options.C: When a positively charged object is momentarily brought into contact with a neutral metallic sphere, the sphere acquires a net positive charge.
options.D: When a plastic rod is rubbed with wool, the two objects acquire a net charge of the same sign.

questions.explanation: When a positively charged object is brought into contact with a neutral metallic sphere, some electrons from the sphere are attracted to the positively charged object, leaving the sphere with a net positive charge. Option A is incorrect: in induction, charge does not flow from the rod to the object; electrons are redistributed. Option B is incorrect: induction with a negatively charged rod results in a net positive charge on the sphere after grounding. Option D is incorrect: rubbing transfers electrons, giving opposite charges.

questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor is charged with a battery. The battery is then disconnected, and a dielectric material is inserted between the plates of the capacitor. Which of the following is correct about the effect of the dielectric?

options.A: The potential difference between the plates remains the same and the charge increases.
options.B: The charge on the plates decreases and the energy stored increases.
options.C: The electric field between the plates and the energy stored decrease.
options.D: The capacitance remains the same and the electric field between the plates increases.

questions.explanation: When the battery is disconnected, the charge on the capacitor remains constant. Inserting a dielectric increases capacitance (C = κC₀). Since Q is constant and C increases, V = Q/C decreases. The electric field E = V/d also decreases. The energy stored U = Q²/(2C) decreases because C increases. Option C correctly states that both the electric field and energy stored decrease.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about the resistance of a conductor with a circular cross-section?

options.A: At a given temperature, the resistance of copper and silver wires of the same length and diameter is the same.
options.B: The resistance of the conductor increases as its length increases and its diameter decreases.
options.C: The resistance of the conductor increases as its length and diameter increases.
options.D: The resistance of the conductor decreases as it is heated.

questions.explanation: Resistance is given by R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity, L is length, and A is cross-sectional area. For a circular conductor, A = πd²/4. As length increases, R increases. As diameter decreases, area decreases, so R increases. Option A is incorrect: copper and silver have different resistivities. Option C is incorrect: increasing diameter decreases resistance. Option D is incorrect: for most conductors, resistance increases with temperature.

questions.question: A student wants to investigate Ohm's law using an ammeter (A) and a voltmeter (V) to measure current through and potential difference across a resistor R. Moreover, she employs a rheostat to vary the potential difference across the resistor. Which of the following connections is the correct set up of the circuit to perform the experiment?

options.A: Diagram A
options.B: Diagram B
options.C: Diagram C
options.D: Diagram D

questions.explanation: To verify Ohm's law, the ammeter must be connected in series with the resistor to measure current, and the voltmeter must be connected in parallel across the resistor to measure potential difference. The rheostat should be in series to vary the current/voltage. The correct connection has the ammeter in series and voltmeter in parallel across the resistor.

questions.question: Circular paths followed by two charges q₁ and q₂ moving with the same speed in uniform magnetic field directed into the page (x) are shown in the figure below. If the two charges have the same mass, which of the following is correct about the sign and the magnitude of charges?

options.A: q₁ is negative, q₂ is positive and |q₁| < |q₂|.
options.B: q₁ is negative, q₂ is positive and |q₁| > |q₂|.
options.C: q₁ is positive, q₂ is negative and |q₁| < |q₂|.
options.D: q₁ is positive, q₂ is negative and |q₁| > |q₂|.

questions.explanation: For a charge moving in a magnetic field directed into the page, the direction of the magnetic force (F = qv × B) determines the direction of the circular path. Using the right-hand rule, a positive charge curves in one direction and a negative charge curves in the opposite direction. The radius of curvature r = mv/(qB). For equal mass and speed, the charge with the smaller radius has the larger magnitude of charge. From the figure, q₁ has a smaller radius, so |q₁| > |q₂|.

questions.question: The primary coil of a transformer has 250 turns and its secondary coil consists of 1500 turns. If 220 V is applied to its primary coil, the voltage induced in the secondary coil and the ratio of current in the primary coil to the current in the secondary coil, respectively, are

options.A: 1320 V and 6
options.B: 1330 V and 6
options.C: 1220 V and 60
options.D: 1320 V and 60

questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. V_s = V_p × N_s/N_p = 220 × 1500/250 = 220 × 6 = 1320 V. The current ratio is inverse of the turns ratio: I_p/I_s = N_s/N_p = 1500/250 = 6. Therefore, the voltage is 1320 V and the current ratio is 6:1. This matches option A.

questions.question: A diode is an electronic component that

options.A: is useful to convert a DC voltage to AC voltage.
options.B: allows electric current to pass through it in one direction.
options.C: allows the flow of current when its p-type region is connected to the negative terminal of a cell.
options.D: allows current to pass through it either from cathode to anode or from anode to cathode.

questions.explanation: A diode is a semiconductor device that allows current to flow in only one direction (forward bias). It acts as a rectifier, converting AC to DC, not DC to AC (option A is incorrect). Option C is incorrect: a diode conducts when the p-type (anode) is connected to the positive terminal, not negative. Option D is incorrect: a diode allows current only in one direction (from anode to cathode).

questions.question: Three forces, each having equal magnitudes of 10 N, are applied to an object on a horizontal surface. A force F₁ makes an angle of 30° above positive x-axis, F₂ makes 30° above the negative x-axis, and the third force F₃ is directed along the positive x-axis. The magnitude and direction of their resultant force are, respectively

options.A: 20 N 45° above positive x-axis.
options.B: 14.1 N in the positive y-axis.
options.C: 20 N in the negative y-axis.
options.D: 14.1 N 45° above positive x-axis.

questions.explanation: Resolve forces: F₁x = 10cos30° = 10(√3/2) = 8.66 N, F₁y = 10sin30° = 5 N. F₂x = -10cos30° = -8.66 N, F₂y = 10sin30° = 5 N. F₃ = 10 N in +x direction. Sum Fx = 8.66 - 8.66 + 10 = 10 N. Sum Fy = 5 + 5 = 10 N. Resultant magnitude = √(10²+10²) = 14.1 N. Direction = tan⁻¹(10/10) = 45° above positive x-axis. So the resultant is 14.1 N at 45° above positive x-axis.

questions.question: A student throws a ball vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. The maximum height reached by the ball and its velocity 3.0 s after it was thrown are, respectively

options.A: 20 m and 30 m/s upward.
options.B: 15 m and 10 m/s downward.
options.C: 105 m and 50 m/s upward.
options.D: 20 m and 10 m/s downward.

questions.explanation: Maximum height: v² = u² + 2as, where v = 0 at maximum height. 0 = (20)² + 2(-9.8)h, h = 400/(19.6) = 20.4 m ≈ 20 m. Velocity at t = 3 s: v = u - gt = 20 - 9.8(3) = 20 - 29.4 = -9.4 m/s ≈ -10 m/s (downward). Therefore, the maximum height is about 20 m and velocity after 3 s is about 10 m/s downward, matching option D.
